Standardized Mean Differences for Covariate Balance

Source: R/balance_diagnostics.R
balance_smd.Rd

Computes the standardized mean difference (SMD) of each covariate between a group and a reference group, before and, when `weights` are given, after weighting (inverse probability of treatment, overlap or matching weights). It is the table behind a Love plot, [plot_balance_love()], and the check that comes with a propensity-score analysis or a table-one of two cohorts.

Usage

balance_smd(
  data,
  group,
  vars = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  denominator = c("pooled", "reference"),
  threshold = 0.1
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

group

Name of the grouping column: two or more levels.

vars

Covariates (column names). Default: every column except `group` and the `weights` column.

weights

`NULL` (default), the name of a numeric column of `data`, or a numeric vector with one weight per row. When given, the table has an `"Adjusted"` row besides the `"Unadjusted"` one for each covariate. Rows with a missing weight are dropped from the Adjusted sample only; the Unadjusted sample keeps them.

ref

The reference level of `group`. Default: the first level (the first value, for a non-factor).

denominator

`"pooled"` (default) or `"reference"` (the standard deviation of the reference group, as for the average treatment effect on the treated).

threshold

The `abs(smd)` below which a covariate is called balanced (default `0.1`).

Value

A tibble of class `balance_smd` with one row per comparison, covariate and sample: `comparison` (`"level vs ref"`), `variable`, `sample` (`"Unadjusted"` / `"Adjusted"`), `mean_ref`, `mean_cmp`, `smd`, `abs_smd`, `var_ratio` (variance in the compared group over the reference group) and `balanced`. The reference level and the threshold are in `attr(x, "ref")` and `attr(x, "threshold")`.

Details

For a numeric covariate the SMD is the difference in means over the pooled standard deviation, `sqrt((s_ref^2 + s_cmp^2) / 2)`. A logical or 0/1 covariate is treated as numeric, so its SMD is the difference in proportions over `sqrt((v_ref + v_cmp) / 2)` with the sample variance. A factor or character covariate becomes one 0/1 indicator per level (named `variable = level`). Variances are the unbiased (sample) ones. With weights, the means in the numerator are weighted but the standard deviation in the denominator is that of the unweighted sample, so the adjusted and unadjusted SMDs are on the same scale (as in `cobalt` and `MatchIt`); `var_ratio` uses the weighted variances. Missing values are dropped covariate by covariate. A common rule of thumb calls `abs(smd) < 0.1` balanced.

See also

[plot_balance_love()]. The `cobalt` package has a fuller set of balance tools (balance after matching and weighting, many weighting estimands); this function needs no extra package and covers the table and the Love plot.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  treated = rep(c("no", "yes"), each = 100),
  age = c(rnorm(100, 60, 10), rnorm(100, 66, 10)),
  male = c(rbinom(100, 1, 0.45), rbinom(100, 1, 0.6)),
  site = sample(c("A", "B", "C"), 200, replace = TRUE)
)
balance_smd(d, "treated")
#> Covariate balance (reference: no); 3 covariate row(s) with |SMD| >= 0.1 in the unadjusted sample
#> # A tibble: 5 × 9
#>   comparison variable sample     mean_ref mean_cmp     smd abs_smd var_ratio
#>   <chr>      <chr>    <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 yes vs no  age      Unadjusted    61.1     65.6   0.488   0.488      1.14 
#> 2 yes vs no  male     Unadjusted     0.42     0.53  0.221   0.221      1.02 
#> 3 yes vs no  site = A Unadjusted     0.31     0.37  0.126   0.126      1.09 
#> 4 yes vs no  site = B Unadjusted     0.36     0.34 -0.0417  0.0417     0.974
#> 5 yes vs no  site = C Unadjusted     0.33     0.29 -0.0861  0.0861     0.931
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: balanced <lgl>
